messages.subject: Re: Problem extracting model results
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

This issue appears to have emerged from Mplus 8.6 adding new section headers to the output for some mixture models. This inevitably generates challenges for the R package that I can only fix reactively (i.e., once people have problems). So, thanks for orienting me to these new sections. I've added code in the github version of the package to handle the new sections and have confirmed that the outputs mentioned above (from the LCA tutorial) parse correctly. You can get the fix with devtools::install_github("michaelhallquist/MplusAutomation")

Best,
Michael

messages.subject: Switching directories in runModels
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
This may be a simple question but it's stumping me, and I wasn't able to find a good way to tackle it.

If I want to run a model that is in folder D:/mplus

runModels("D:/mplus")

I get an error because the command generated is

C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe /c cd "D:\mplus" && "Mplus" "1-class LCA 6.2.inp"

When it should be

C:\WINDOWS\system32\cmd.exe cd /d "D:\mplus" && "Mplus" "1-class LCA 6.2.inp"
to allow the directories to change from C: to D:

However putting /d in
runModels("/d D:/mplus") doesn't work. Does anyone know any other options?

messages.subject: Re: Generating Data in Mplus and Analyzing them in R
messages.subject_clean: Generating Data in Mplus and Analyzing them in R
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dora,

This is outside the scope of what the MplusAutomation package is specifically intended to accomplish. That said, I would take a look at list.files() and lapply() in base R, and rbindlist() and fread() in the data.table package. If you put those together, it's easy to read and combine large numbers of files. Something like this:

flist <- list.files(path=getwd())
res <- data.table::rbindlist(lapply(flist, data.table::fread))

Hope that helps,
Michael

messages.subject: quick and easy question regarding extracting multiple confidence intervals from logistic regressions
messages.subject_clean: quick and easy question regarding extracting multiple confidence intervals from logistic regressions
messages.body_plain:
Hi folks,
I'm trying to fix some old code in which I extract confidence intenrvals from multiple files in a directory.
I had tried
modelResults <- extractModelParameters("mydirectory",recursive=TRUE)
based on the documentation at
https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/MplusAutomation/vignettes/Vignette.pdf
This generates the message, though:
extractModelParameters has been deprecated. Please use readModels("NameofMplusOutfileDirectory", what="parameters")$parameters to replicate the old functionality.
but when I try:
paramsnew <- readModels(" NameofMplusOutfileDirectory  ",recursive=TRUE, what="parameters$ci.stdyx.standardized")
or other permutations, I don't seem to recover them. I'm assuming the $parameters in the console message is some typo.
Any hints, gang? TIA! Phil

messages.subject: Re: quick and easy question regarding extracting multiple confidence intervals from logistic regressions
messages.subject_clean: quick and easy question regarding extracting multiple confidence intervals from logistic regressions
messages.body_plain:
Hi Phil,

I think you need something like

paramsnew <- readModels("NameofMplusOutfileDirectory",recursive=TRUE, what="parameters”)

Then, for each file, you should have:

paramsnew[[1]]$parameters$ci.stdyx.standardized

And you can assemble these with

lapply(paramsnew, function(x) { x$parameters$ci.stdyx.standardized })

Hope this helps!
Michael

messages.subject: Extracting tech3
messages.body_plain:
Dear Michael and Joshua,

unfortunately I cant parse tech3 output from my files.
readModels() yields either an empty list or an error (<simpleError in extractTech3(outfiletext, fileInfo, curfile): Object 'fileInfo' not found>), depending on the model.
The covariance matrices are present in Mplus, of course.

My setup:
Tested with Mplus 7 and 8.4
Tested simple CFA models (-> empty list) as well as a sort of experimental moderated non-linear factor models (-> error). Those include some model constraints. If you need input on the latter, see Bauer (2017) or I could attach the output.
Things I looked up:
https://groups.google.com/g/mplusautomation/c/K49IPkhV7FE/m/Ksm1AYB8AjcJ, I couldnt get the suggestion with SAVEDATA to work.
directly messing around with extractTech3() didnt help either.
I would be gratefull if you have a quick idea what's going wrong (or what I am doing wrong). Otherwise I will go down the path of writing something up on my own.

Thanks!

References:
Bauer, D. J. (2017). A more general model for testing measurement invariance and differential item functioning. Psychological methods, 22(3), 507.

messages.subject: mplusModeler with multiple imputed datasets
messages.body_plain:
Dear everyone,

I am trying to run a few models using the mplusObject and mplusModeler functions and it seems I cant get them to work with multiple imputed datasets. Creating the 15 imputed datasets as well as the .dat file with the list of imputed datasets works well, but in the generated .inp script, it seems to use the wrong dataset name (without "implist"). I also get this result when I use the example from the CRAN manual (p.48). When I use the version from github, I get a different error message from mplusModeler, but it still doesn't work (Assertion on 'df' failed: Must be of type 'data.frame', not 'list'):

> idat <- list(data.frame(mpg = mtcars$mpg, hp = c(100, mtcars$hp[-1])),
+              data.frame(mpg = mtcars$mpg, hp = c(110, mtcars$hp[-1])),
+              data.frame(mpg = mtcars$mpg, hp = c(120, mtcars$hp[-1])))

> testobjimp <- mplusObject(MODEL = "[mpg];", rdata = idat, imputed = TRUE)
R variables selected automatically as any variable name that
occurs in the MODEL, VARIABLE, or DEFINE section.

> testimp <- mplusModeler(testobjimp,modelout = "testimp.inp",writeData = "ifmissing", hashfilename=TRUE,run = TRUE)
Wrote model to: testimp.inp
Fehler in .cleanHashData(df = df, keepCols = keepCols, dropCols = dropCols,  :
  Assertion on 'df' failed: Must be of type 'data.frame', not 'list'.

Has anyone else experienced this and could help me?

Best regards and thanks in advance

Malte
